---
16:Every visual, audio and UI system in the game is a kernel subscriber, and eleven approved GDDs each restate "marks dirty in the notification, draws in the render callback, writes only engine-side nodes" without a single place that fixes what that means in code, in which order the presenters run, how a fractional simulation position becomes a whole base pixel, or which class may submit commands. This ADR fixes one contract: subscriber handlers only mark dirty and return `ctx.complete()`; one `PresentationDriver` runs every presenter once per rendered frame in a fixed named stage order and hands them one `PresentFrame`; every moving thing is placed by the single function `Placement.at` (`floori` of the lerp at `tick_alpha`) with `physics_interpolation` pinned off; presentation holds only non-persisted scalars that are reset on a restore edge; and `INPUT_SURFACE` is the only class that can be issued submit rights, which still require a `SurfaceHandle`.
34:| **Enables** | ADR-0008 (the `PresentFrame` and driver the Pipeline root hosts; the `frame_pre_draw` write), ADR-0019 (Adapter and Presenter split), ADR-0024 (Filter facet and truth-channel reads), ADR-0028 (Lighting is a stage and a write allow-list), ADR-0029 (Audio is a stage), ADR-0030 (HUD and menus are stages and INPUT_SURFACE objects), ADR-0031 (DIAGNOSTIC facet), ADR-0034 (PROJECTOR class rules; shape and Y-sort are its own). |
90:           PresentFrame.alpha / T / running / present_time   read once, shared by all stages     (§ 3, § 4)
91:           if clock.load_seq changed -> every presenter.on_discontinuity(RESTORE)                  (§ 6)
92:           stage  0 PROJECT        PROJECTOR builds / rebuilds (chunked)
93:                  1 CAMERA_SOLVE   CameraSolver: pose_q, world_to_hud (no canvas write yet)
112:class_name PresentationFacet extends RefCounted
125:| `PRESENTATION` | Camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Lighting, Failure & Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, the Filter's host object | `PresentationViews` of SIM blocks (previous and current pairs), `PresentationClock`, the frame's `PresentFrame`, frozen content catalogs, **products of strictly earlier stages** (§ 3), the Filter's `perceived()` for corruptible values | Only the allow-list below | Never. The facet has no submit method. |
134:- Presentation never reads another presenter's private state. A presenter may call a getter on a **strictly earlier stage's** product (the camera pose, the beam pose, the decoy list). Each presenter declares `reads: Array[int]` of stage ids at registration and the driver's freeze check fails boot if any entry is not strictly less than the presenter's own stage. A visual presenter never reads the Audio presenter or any audio level, bus meter, cue or voice state (TR-audio-042); Audio is stage 8 and nothing reads from it.
176:### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages
178:**A single `PresentationHost` node** (`extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code) owns a `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls `driver.frame(...)` from its `_process`. The host is the Pipeline root or a node it owns (ADR-0008 decides which; either way exactly one node). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.
183:# src/presentation/presentation_stage.gd. Named constants only; nobody writes a literal stage number.
184:class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted
186:const CAMERA_SOLVE: int = 1    # CameraSolver computes pose_q and world_to_hud; the canvas write is in frame_pre_draw
198:- HUD AC-HS-89 and TR-hud-022: camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting. Stages 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.
199:- PF-35 and TR-percfilter-025: Avatar, then Filter, then Lighting reads the decoy list. Stages 2, 3, 6.
200:- TR-pc-040: the Presenter's beam pose is written before Lighting applies. Stages 2, 6.
201:- Instruments call `perceived()`, so they follow the Filter. Stages 3, 4.
203:- **Camera versus Avatar.** Pipeline C2 asks for the camera "ordered after the actor" so that both compose the same interpolated position. This ADR gets the same guarantee by construction, not by order: the solver and the Avatar Presenter both call `Placement.at` with the same `PresentFrame` values, so they cannot disagree. The solver runs first because the HUD needs `world_to_hud` before it draws (TR-hud-022). Step 12 of the pipeline spike (zero render-px disagreement) tests the claim.
206:class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted
208:var stage: int                        # a PresentationStage constant
209:var reads: Array[int]                 # stages whose products this presenter calls; each must be < stage
210:var present: Callable                 # (frame: PresentFrame) -> void
211:var on_discontinuity: Callable        # (kind: int) -> void; DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE or DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT
213:class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted     # one object, reused every frame; fields overwritten, never reallocated
220:class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted
222:func freeze() -> void                                      # sorts by stage; checks reads < stage; unique names; fails boot otherwise
223:func frame(host_delta: float, present_time: float) -> void # fills PresentFrame, handles load_seq, runs the stages
224:func notify_camera_cut() -> void                           # called by the camera stage; next frame every presenter gets CAMERA_CUT
227:`present` and `on_discontinuity` are registered `Callable`s returning `void`. They are **not** kernel-invoked owner callables, so ADR-0003's `CompletionToken` rule does not apply to them, and registering `Callable`s rather than overriding a base class avoids the 4.7 typed-return override rule altogether (ADR-0003 § 1 makes the same choice for owners). If ADR-0010 picks an `@abstract` base class instead, `-> void` overrides need no `return`.
229:**Driver rules.** The driver iterates a fixed-size array, allocates nothing, checks `present.is_valid()` before each call and skips and counts a freed presenter (`PRESENTER_DEAD`, as ADR-0002 does for result handlers), and **never runs a presenter inside a tick**. Presenter faults cannot fault the kernel: nothing here runs in a tick phase. Stage timing exists in dev and playtest builds through ADR-0001's diagnostics timer and is compiled out of release.
231:**The frame object is the clock.** `PresentFrame.alpha` is read once; no presenter reads `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` directly (a lint on `tick_alpha` outside the driver, the camera solver's pure-function twin and tests). This guarantees one alpha per frame. A presenter may read `frame.T` for values the simulation also computes (the beacon aim at `T`, a Graph step index); it **must never** use `T` or any tick counter as cosmetic phase (registry `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`), and uses `frame.present_time` for cosmetic phase.
233:**Pause.** `PresentFrame.present_time` is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED` and `alpha` is 1.0, so a presenter that computes from `present_time` and `alpha` is frozen without being told. Layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table) keep running on engine time because they must respond while paused (PR-9); they are INPUT_SURFACE objects and UI Controls, not world presenters.
241:class_name Placement extends RefCounted
242:## Interpolate previous to current at alpha, then floor, per axis. alpha is clamped by the caller's PresentFrame.
284:3. it is reset by `on_discontinuity` on a restore, a new game, a camera cut and `hard_start` (TR-instr-002, TR-attention-047);
287:**A presenter's drawn output is a pure function** of `(PresentationViews at this frame, PresentFrame, its resettable scalars)`. The first frame after a restore needs no special path: `ALL` rebuilds from views, `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` clears the scalars, and the kernel's `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so there is no interpolation across the break (TR-cmd-046, TR-horror-041, TR-attention-047, TR-webmap-039 restore half). A multi-beat stall plays at most one beat and never replays (TR-attention-047): a presenter keeps the last-seen sequence value it was shown, compares it with the view's, and on a jump of more than one shows the end state.
289:**Edge detection by sequence counters.** A presenter detects a discrete source change by comparing a view's sequence counter to the value it last saw (`breath_src_change_seq`, TR-suit-041), not by counting notifications, because merged delivery turns N ticks into one batch. Because the notification, the dirty mark and the draw happen in one rendered frame, a click can start in the Audio stage and the dial swap land in the Instruments stage of the same frame.
299:At the top of `frame(...)` the driver compares `clock.load_seq` with the last seen value and, on a change, calls every presenter's `on_discontinuity(DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE)` **before** any `present`. Camera cuts arrive the other way: the camera stage calls `driver.notify_camera_cut()` and the next frame delivers `DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT` (reset of instrument scalars and cull history; Instruments IW-33). `BODY_TRANSFER` is a rebase, not a cut, unless the new body's limits clamp (TR-shipbody-049, ADR-0008). If ADR-0001's owner declines the extra field, the equivalent is a composition-root-owned counter on the same clock object (ADR-0004's draft has no restore marker in `ChangeBatch`; its `is_all` on load is the same value as a mass change); the driver is the only consumer either way, so the choice does not leak into presenters.
305:- **Where a submit call may occur.** An `INPUT_SURFACE` object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` submits from **its own `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`**, exactly as the Input Adapter does (ADR-0001 § 2 already lets any registered INPUT_SURFACE node run below `TICK_DRIVER`, and § 3 puts the Adapter there). A UI surface (Chart Table menus later, the Interaction prompt if it ever submits) **latches an intent in a plain field in its UI callback** and submits it from that `_process`, so its commands are queued before the driver's tick loop and reach the same tick as the Adapter's. It **never** calls `submit` from an engine signal handler, `_gui_input`, `_input`, `_physics_process`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object (ADR-0001 guideline restated). The control plane is different: `ControlHandle` calls are recorded when made, from any phase (CR-15), so a UI button calling `PauseGate` from its signal handler is legal. This ADR therefore adds no second submit location and no driver stage for submission.
306:- **Result handlers.** The kernel flushes the result buffer in the driver, before presentation; an `INPUT_SURFACE` result handler is a kernel-invoked callable and obeys the same contract as a subscriber handler: it records the result into a fixed ring and returns `ctx.complete()`. Display of a rejection happens in the object's own presenter step (the stage it is registered for), never in the handler.
312:Engine signals (`signal`, `.connect(...)`) are used **between presentation objects for user-initiated events only** (a card opens, a setting changes, a button is pressed). They are never the kernel's notification transport (ADR-0004 § 1 decides a kernel-owned observer registry of Callables and no engine signals; this ADR agrees), never carry simulation values into a simulation module, and are never declared or connected in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/` (a lint; the simulation is scene-tree free). A signal is not a way around the stage-read rule: a presenter that needs another presenter's per-frame product reads it through a declared `reads` edge, not through a connection.

The `_process` rule applies to objects registered through a `PresenterDescriptor`; the exemptions are `PresentationHost` (and the Pipeline root that may host it), `INPUT_SURFACE` objects at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`, and layer 3 and 4 UI Controls (PR-9).

131:2. **Cast** through the table's schema. JSON numbers arrive as `float` (CONTENT-EXP-1 c). `IntField.read(value, lo, hi)` accepts a `TYPE_INT`, or a `TYPE_FLOAT` that is integral (`value == floorf(value)`) and strictly below 2^53 in magnitude (`absf(value) < 9007199254740992.0`); a fractional value or a `TYPE_BOOL` is `CONTENT_FIELD_TYPE`, a magnitude at or above 2^53 is `CONTENT_INT_PRECISION` (the bound is exclusive because `9007199254740993` silently parses to 2^53), outside `lo..hi` is `CONTENT_FIELD_RANGE`. A designer-facing fractional field (a 1.5-tile radius) is declared `SCALED` with a `scale` and converted once by `roundi(x * scale)` (half away from zero, negatives included); the lint `FLOAT_ROUND_AMBIGUOUS` rejects a value whose scaled form lies within 1e-6 of a .5 boundary.
136:**Closed schemas live in code as literal rows.** A schema is part of the program, so it is GDScript, not data, under `src/data/<domain>/<table>_schema.gd`. GDScript `const` cannot hold constructed objects, so the schema is a `const` array of plain literal rows (`[name, kind, lo, hi, required, unit, scale]`), turned into typed `FieldSpec` objects by `static func fields() -> Array[FieldSpec]` when the loader starts. There is no `static var`; a static, immutable schema is not what `kernel_autoload_or_global` forbids (that rule covers access to the kernel, blocks and views). `kind` is one of `INT`, `SCALED`, `ENUM_ID`, `STRING_ID`, `INT_ARRAY`, `ROWS`. An unknown key is `CONTENT_FIELD_UNKNOWN`; a key on the domain's forbidden list (horror: `damage`, `accuracy`, `armour`, `dps`, `xp`, `unlock`, `health`, `hp`, `kill`, `loot`, `threat`, `aggro`, `hate`; items: price, rarity, recipe; interaction: stats, cooldown, reward) is `CONTENT_FIELD_FORBIDDEN`. The forbidden check runs before the unknown-key check, so the code names the intent. The only permitted non-schema key is `"_note"`, a string stripped by the loader and never hashed. Named structural invariants (§ 2.5) are declared in the same schema file.
145:- **Nested-row tables** (items, templates, world records, instrument and lie-target rows) use a typed `RefCounted` row class (`ItemDef`, `RoomTemplate`...). **Flat scalar tables** (`GraphTuning`, `hud_tuning`, Attention and Save/Load knobs) use one generic `ScalarTable` built from the schema, exposing named `int` getters; they do not each need a row class.
179:- **File-pure rules** are a deterministic function of the content files and `content_lint_config` (rows `{name, value, owner, status: LOCKED | PLACEHOLDER}`). They run in `tools/ci/content_lint.gd` through the same `ContentLoader`, so parsing and schemas are never reimplemented. Output is ordered by `(template_id, lint_id, record_key)`; a waiver needs a recorded reason and no waiver may name `STORY_SLOT_FILLED_IN_MVP` (TR-derelict-024). rng(208, 216, """**6.1 The camera is a pure solver run in the `CAMERA_SOLVE` stage (TR-pxl-010, 011, 012, 013, 015; the formulas D.6 to D.10 are the GDD's).** `CameraSolver` is a `RefCounted` with `solve(input: SolverInput, state: SolverState, params: SolverParams) -> Pose`, no scene-tree dependency, float64 per-axis state held as scalars (not `Vector2`), `dt` clamped to `DT_MAX` (0.05 s). The **type of `SolverInput` is the enforcement of Camera C1**: it carries only the follow target's previous and current body-local positions, `tick_alpha`, the raw local beam aim, the zoom step, `dt`, and cut / rebase flags; it has no field through which Attention, breach, horrors, sound, the graph or sanity could enter, so the same input trace gives the same camera trace in calm, tell and breach by construction. The Perception Filter has no write path to a camera or viewport property (§ 2.6). The camera is a `PresenterDescriptor` registered at `PresentationStage.CAMERA_SOLVE` (stage 1, ADR-0009 § 3): it calls `solve` once per frame from `driver.frame` and **publishes `pose_q`, the follow pose `f_q`, the jolt offset, the parallax offsets and the `world_to_hud` inputs** to `CameraHost` and `RenderLayout` before the Avatar, Filter, HUD and Lighting stages run. Solver parameters (`tau_follow`, `DT_MAX`) and `ZOOM_MIN_K` are the `RenderTuning` table loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline and injected (schema in Key Interfaces). Camera state is never persisted.

*Restore and discontinuity.* The kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every interpolated block on each transition into `RUNNING` (ADR-0001 § 4, ADR-0003), so the first frame after a restore interpolates nothing; that is the **only** restore-continuity mechanism and this ADR adds no owner-side rule. The camera stage additionally **CUTs** the solver (starting with `L = 0` easing in) in its `on_discontinuity(DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE)`, which ADR-0009's driver delivers when `PresentationClock.load_seq` changes (the kernel increments it on every `LOADING → RUNNING` transition, restore and new game, never on `PAUSED` or `SAVING → RUNNING`; ADR-0001 amendment batch). A pod or transit body transfer is a CUT; a weld or detach `BODY_TRANSFER` carrying `frame_delta_px` calls `rebase(frame_delta_px)`, which shifts the follow and history and keeps lag and `L`.

**6.2 The frame model and the hook.** `PipelineRoot` **is** ADR-0009's single `PresentationHost` (closing ADR-0009 OQ-E, OQ-J and OQ-L): no other node hosts the driver, and because every step below runs inside one function, no priority tie and no tree-order dependency exists. The composition root constructs the `PresentationDriver` and injects it; `PipelineRoot` holds it. Its single `_process`, at `ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, runs in this fixed order: (1) advance `present_time` (§ 6.3); (2) the zoom cooldown (§ 3.1); (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty (§ 3.2); (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`, which runs the stages with `CAMERA_SOLVE` first. The `CameraHost` (a top-level presentation node under `PipelineRoot`, never a child of a body) connects one handler to **`RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw`**. The handler does exactly two writes from already-solved values and nothing else: the world viewport's `canvas_transform` (from `pose_q` plus the jolt offset) and the parallax layer offsets (integer offsets the camera stage computed with `Placement`'s integer helpers, `floori`, not a bare `-floor(...)`). The handler therefore runs after the HUD stage, so a solve inside it would leave `world_to_hud`, the Avatar presenter's beam pose and `mouse_to_world_aim` one frame behind the world: a permanent HUD-versus-world disagreement on exactly the "screen is still when the ship is still" surface (PR-6 C11, TR-pxl-019). Step (1) of `_process` advances it by the `_process` delta while `PresentationClock.state` is `RUNNING`, `SAVING`, or `LOADING` with the hold shown, and leaves it frozen while `PAUSED`; it is **never scaled by reduced motion** (reduced motion scales individual effects). *Why the solve is not in the handler.* Probed ordering (windowed 4.7.2 editor, Forward+, main thread, `thread_model` 1 and 2): all node `_process`, then `frame_pre_draw`, then `frame_post_draw`; a `canvas_transform` written in the handler is the one drawn that frame, and a write from `_process` is also drawn that frame. Solving in the `_process` pass also keeps the solver unit-testable without a signal that never fires headless.

*Verification status (TD-20).* Windowed 4.7.2 editor: all node `_process`, then `frame_pre_draw`, then `frame_post_draw` (probed); it fires only when a frame is drawn (never headless). Release export, Direct3D 12, the Steam Deck, a minimised or occluded window and `low_processor_mode` are UNVERIFIED (pipeline spike step 12 re-runs the same probe on a release export). `rendering/driver/threads/thread_model` is pinned at 1 (§ 5.1; value 2 unsupported) so the probed ordering holds. **Fallback, used only if `frame_pre_draw` fails the release-export spike:** the canvas write moves to the last statement of `PipelineRoot._process`, after `driver.frame(...)`. ### 1. Frame update path

One rendered frame. The tick is driven from `_process`, never from the physics callback (kernel CR-1a; see Open Question OQ-1 for three GDDs that still cite the physics callback).

```
Engine frame (_process order by process_priority)
│
├─ INPUT_ADAPTER (-100)  Input Adapter (INPUT_SURFACE; the only presentation-side node below the driver's priority, so the KRN-LAT-02 priority lint exempts INPUT_SURFACE nodes)
│     read InputMap actions → change-only intents (set_move_intent, set_aim ≤ every 3 ticks)
│     → kernel.submit(type, payload, actor, correlation)            [sync call, queued]
│
├─ TICK_DRIVER (-50)  KernelHost → TickDriver (the only wall-clock read that reaches the sim)
│     boundary service first (SAVING / LOADING / pause / resume; a frame that ends in a transition into RUNNING clears the accumulator and discards its own delta)
│     then, while RUNNING: acc += delta_us × TICK_RATE ; ticks = min(floor(acc / 1e6), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME=4)
│     repeat ticks times: Kernel.step()  ──► P0 Begin
│                                           P1 Intake   (queue → this tick's batch, coalesce intents)
│                                           P2 Dispatch (authority check → validate → apply in WriteScope)
│                                           P3 Step     (hooks whose T mod divisor == offset, topo order)
│                                           P4 Commit
│                                           P5 Notify   (batches queued; PRESENTATION merged per frame)
│                                           P6 Boundary (snapshot/restore/pause requests)
│     drop lag (LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS 0) ; flush results ; compute tick_alpha
│
└─ priority 2  Presentation subscribers (render callback)
      handlers only mark dirty → draw using read views at tick_alpha:
      pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) × tick_alpha)
      Avatar Presenter → Lighting → Trail → Instruments (perceived()) → HUD (perceived()) → Audio
      Pipeline root: CameraSolver → canvas_transform in frame_pre_draw
```

    description: "Only PipelineRoot and ViewportWiring (src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd) write SubViewport.size and size_2d_override*, the world container's position, scale, stretch_shrink and material, any CanvasLayer scale, offset or transform, and HudRoot.size; only the CameraHost frame_pre_draw handler writes the world canvas_transform and the parallax offsets; no subscriber, the Filter, Lighting, HUD or Chart Table writes a viewport or camera property; no code but RenderLayout.derive computes k, H, world_to_hud or the cursor mapping."

decisions.chosen: Option (a): use_hdr_2d=false at MVP, container material null, flat-palette guarantee kept; option (b) specified as a gated contingency (resolve material included by the Filter shader, gated on the effective rendering method, D_filter becomes 1)
decisions.reason: Probed: an HDR viewport through a container on the SDR root outputs unconverted linear colour ((128,64,200) reads (55,13,147)); the resolve fix is renderer-specific (double-converts under Compatibility). (a) keeps every other ADR rule consistent until lighting spike steps 7 and 8 prove HDR is needed.

decisions.point: Presentation host and camera solve placement (E2, T1, TD-03)
decisions.chosen: PipelineRoot is the single PresentationHost; one _process at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION runs present_time, zoom cooldown, RESCALING, driver.frame; CameraSolver.solve is the CAMERA_SOLVE stage; frame_pre_draw only writes canvas_transform and parallax offsets; PRESENTATION_LATE withdrawn
decisions.reason: Probed: frame_pre_draw fires after every _process, so a solve inside it would leave the HUD, beam pose and aim mapping one frame behind the world; this also removes the priority tie and keeps the solver unit-testable headless.

decisions.chosen: Distinct indices: hold 1, HUD 2, MenuPixel 3, MenuReading 4, Debug 5
decisions.reason: Removes the dependency on a sibling-order tie-break that is fragile to reparenting; no test needed.

decisions.chosen: Pipeline GDD D.16 owns the figures; ADR-0008 7 owns the rules and keeps a mirrored table; container composite is its own row; D_root 63 and 93; DrawBudget.validate dropped
decisions.reason: A Foundation ADR must not churn after every spike measurement; the composite draw is counted on the root (probed). A separate frame-budget.md was out of scope for a single-file pass.

decisions.chosen: Pass A built at MVP behind ViewportWiring.Mode, a constructor argument; pass B and the A/B equivalence test are built only if lighting spike step 2 adopts B; debug tree walk is an optional later story
decisions.reason: A GDScript const cannot be varied in a test, and B is not yet adopted.

decisions.chosen: fallback_to_opengl3=false and fallback_to_d3d12=false are required project.godot keys; a release-build method/driver mismatch is a fatal unsupported-GPU screen; thread_model held at 1
decisions.reason: The engine defaults all fallbacks to true and would silently ship a Compatibility look; the probed hook ordering was observed under thread_model 1 and 2 but only 1 is pinned.

decisions.point: Display settings persistence and kernel state (T2, T3, TD-04, TD-26)
decisions.chosen: DisplaySettings persisted host-locally by the Chart Table SettingsStore (CT-19, ADR-0030); ADR-0006 is not a dependency; kernel state and the restore CUT come from PresentationClock.state and load_seq; no KernelStateView
decisions.reason: Settings are per-install, not PROFILE or WORLD scope, and ADR-0006 ships zero PROFILE blocks at MVP; the ADR-0001 amendment batch supplies the read-only fields.

decisions.chosen: Only mechanism is the kernel's snap_baseline on entry to RUNNING plus the camera CUT on DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE; the post_restore/ADR-0016 rule is dropped
decisions.reason: Two mechanisms for one guarantee invite double handling or skipped owners.

decisions.chosen: File grew from about 95 KB to about 161 KB, mostly the mandated Registry Candidates section (TD-33) and the added probe record
decisions.reason: T7 flagged size; the growth is required content, not a decline, and the section can be trimmed once the orchestrator merges the candidates into the registry.

OQ-B: scaled stretch=false SubViewportContainer sampling for textured content, a one-pixel checker, pass B (if built), an odd window size, fractional container position, Compatibility and a release export (flat fill already passes).

OQ-C: the reference says D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6, but a key-absent 4.7.2 project reports vulkan; likely a new-project-template value (UNVERIFIED); reference corrections suggested for modules/rendering.md and breaking-changes.md.

OQ-G (this ADR's letter): whether a disabled viewport holds its last texture when no resize occurs (the PAUSED_FROZEN hold); the resize case is resolved by probe. Not to be confused with ADR-0009's OQ-G/OQ-A letters.

OQ-H: whether the ambient floor and glow can be met with the world viewport SDR, or require use_hdr_2d=true with the section 2.4 resolve material (lighting spike steps 7 and 8); art bible 8.4 and the Lighting GDD need the matching correction.

External dependency (not an OQ): ADR-0001's amendment batch must land PresentationClock.state, PresentationClock.load_seq and ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE before this ADR can be Accepted; ADR-0007, ADR-0009 and ADR-0010 must be Accepted or co-accepted.

Routing note: TD-22's references to OQ-G (TR-pc-039) going to the Player Controller GDD owner and OQ-A's GDD half going to the HUD GDD owner are ADR-0009's OQ letters, not this ADR's, so this pass did not route them.

Release export, Direct3D 12, Steam Deck, a minimised or occluded window and low_processor_mode remain UNVERIFIED for the frame_pre_draw hook (pipeline spike step 12); all draw-call and timing figures remain unmeasured.

registry_candidates.name: renderer_and_windows_driver
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: renderer_and_windows_driver
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed; PROVISIONAL until lighting spike steps 1, 2, 9 and pipeline spike steps 11, 12
    api: "rendering/renderer/rendering_method = forward_plus; rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = vulkan and driver.linuxbsd = vulkan, asserted by effective ProjectSettings value in CI and by the live driver name at boot; required keys fallback_to_opengl3 = false and fallback_to_d3d12 = false (fallback_to_vulkan = false if the D3D12 reversal is taken); rendering/driver/threads/thread_model held at default 1 and asserted; a release build treats a method or driver mismatch as a fatal unsupported-GPU screen"
    not: "Compatibility or Mobile renderer; Direct3D 12 on Windows unless the spike tie-break fires (Vulkan fails a correctness check D3D12 passes, or D3D12 beats Vulkan P99 CPU frame time by >= 10 % on RM-DESKTOP); relying on the engine default driver; silent driver fallback; thread_model 2; a release build that logs a wrong method and continues"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    reason: "Forward+ for Light2D and glow parity and the gated HDR contingency (Compatibility ignores use_hdr_2d, probed); RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK are specified in Vulkan terms; a key-absent project reports vulkan on 4.7.2 (windowed probe) while the reference says D3D12 since 4.6, so only an effective-value assertion is safe; the fallback keys default true and would silently ship a Compatibility look"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: world_viewport_wiring
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: world_viewport_wiring
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    api: "Root Window content_scale_mode DISABLED; world SubViewport (size field_px under pass A, field_px * k_z with size_2d_override = field_px and size_2d_override_stretch = true under pass B; use_hdr_2d = false at MVP; UPDATE_ONCE mandatory on any resize while UPDATE_DISABLED, desired mode tracked in ViewportWiring) inside a SubViewportContainer (stretch false, scale (k_z, k_z) under A, texture_filter NEAREST, material null at MVP); CanvasLayers hold 1, HUD 2 (scale (H, H)), MenuPixel 3, MenuReading 4, Debug 5, distinct indices; ViewportWiring.Mode {A, B} is a constructor argument, pass A built at MVP; all written only by PipelineRoot / ViewportWiring"
    not: "root canvas_items / integer stretch to obtain k, H or k_z; SubViewportContainer.stretch_shrink as the primary (floors, 3840/7 gives 548); a pass-B viewport sized to the window (an override that does not divide the size gives a non-integer scale); a Control under the world viewport; two CanvasLayers sharing an index; reading render_target_update_mode back as state; Mode as a const read inside the class"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    reason: "Probed: root integer stretch is exact only at H = k and the default zoom; CanvasLayer.scale and a stretch=false container scale give exact independent integers; an override that does not divide the size gives 2.0029 not 2; a resize of a disabled viewport blanks it; same-index layers rely on a sibling-order tie-break"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: camera_canvas_transform_write
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: camera_canvas_transform_write
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed; ordering probed on a 4.7.2 dev build, release export UNVERIFIED (spike step 12)
    api: "CameraSolver.solve runs in the CAMERA_SOLVE stage (ADR-0009 stage 1) of PipelineRoot._process and publishes pose_q, f_q, jolt, parallax offsets and the world_to_hud inputs; the CameraHost RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw handler only writes the world SubViewport canvas_transform and the parallax offsets from the solved values (idempotent, branch-free, safe if skipped); primary variant has no Camera2D in the world tree; fallback if step 12 rejects the hook: the write moves to the last statement of PipelineRoot._process after driver.frame (no new ProcessPriority constant)"
    not: "solving inside the frame_pre_draw handler (HUD, Avatar presenter and mouse_to_world_aim would read the previous frame's pose); a Camera2D scroll on its own clock; Camera2D.limit_*; a camera parented to a body; any writer other than the pipeline root, ViewportWiring or the camera host; subscribers drawing from their own _process; ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION_LATE"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    reason: "Probed: frame_pre_draw fires after every _process and before the draw, so a solve in it is invisible to the HUD stage; a write in the handler or in _process is drawn the same frame"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: viewport_geometry_written_outside_pipeline_root
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: viewport_geometry_written_outside_pipeline_root
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    description: "Only PipelineRoot and ViewportWiring (src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd) write SubViewport.size and size_2d_override*, the world container's position, scale, stretch_shrink and material, any CanvasLayer scale, offset or transform, and HudRoot.size; only the CameraHost frame_pre_draw handler writes the world canvas_transform and the parallax offsets; no subscriber, the Filter, Lighting, HUD or Chart Table writes a viewport or camera property; no code but RenderLayout.derive computes k, H, world_to_hud or the cursor mapping."
    why: "Two writers or a re-derived projection produce fractional transforms and disagreeing HUD anchors (TR-pxl-003, TR-pxl-019); the pixel-integrity promise needs one source."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: root_stretch_or_camera2d_zoom_for_scale
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: root_stretch_or_camera2d_zoom_for_scale
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    description: "No root canvas_items or integer stretch to obtain k, H or k_z; no Camera2D.zoom, no tweened or non-integer scale, no Control.scale on HUD nodes, no scale animation anywhere in the world or HUD."
    why: "Root stretch is exact only when H equals k at the default zoom (probed), so it cannot host the Deck's world 2x and HUD 3x; non-integer scale is the failure the pipeline exists to prevent."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: control_or_reading_text_under_world_or_scaled_layer
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: control_or_reading_text_under_world_or_scaled_layer
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    description: "No Control and no node in group hud under the world SubViewport; no reading-face (vector) text under an integer-scaled CanvasLayer or the world container; reading-face text lives on a scale (1,1) layer (MenuReadingLayer, layer 4) with sizes in screen px; HUD text uses bitmap faces or configured oversampling."
    why: "A Control under the world receives world light and the Filter (HR-1); text under an integer scale is bitmap-stretched and blurs."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: camera_solve_inside_frame_pre_draw

decisions.chosen: Option (a): use_hdr_2d=false at MVP, container material null, flat-palette guarantee kept; option (b) specified as a gated contingency (resolve material included by the Filter shader, gated on the effective rendering method, D_filter becomes 1)
decisions.reason: Probed: an HDR viewport through a container on the SDR root outputs unconverted linear colour ((128,64,200) reads (55,13,147)); the resolve fix is renderer-specific (double-converts under Compatibility). (a) keeps every other ADR rule consistent until lighting spike steps 7 and 8 prove HDR is needed.

decisions.point: Presentation host and camera solve placement (E2, T1, TD-03)
decisions.chosen: PipelineRoot is the single PresentationHost; one _process at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION runs present_time, zoom cooldown, RESCALING, driver.frame; CameraSolver.solve is the CAMERA_SOLVE stage; frame_pre_draw only writes canvas_transform and parallax offsets; PRESENTATION_LATE withdrawn
decisions.reason: Probed: frame_pre_draw fires after every _process, so a solve inside it would leave the HUD, beam pose and aim mapping one frame behind the world; this also removes the priority tie and keeps the solver unit-testable headless.

decisions.chosen: Distinct indices: hold 1, HUD 2, MenuPixel 3, MenuReading 4, Debug 5
decisions.reason: Removes the dependency on a sibling-order tie-break that is fragile to reparenting; no test needed.

decisions.chosen: Pipeline GDD D.16 owns the figures; ADR-0008 7 owns the rules and keeps a mirrored table; container composite is its own row; D_root 63 and 93; DrawBudget.validate dropped
decisions.reason: A Foundation ADR must not churn after every spike measurement; the composite draw is counted on the root (probed). A separate frame-budget.md was out of scope for a single-file pass.

decisions.chosen: Pass A built at MVP behind ViewportWiring.Mode, a constructor argument; pass B and the A/B equivalence test are built only if lighting spike step 2 adopts B; debug tree walk is an optional later story
decisions.reason: A GDScript const cannot be varied in a test, and B is not yet adopted.

decisions.chosen: fallback_to_opengl3=false and fallback_to_d3d12=false are required project.godot keys; a release-build method/driver mismatch is a fatal unsupported-GPU screen; thread_model held at 1
decisions.reason: The engine defaults all fallbacks to true and would silently ship a Compatibility look; the probed hook ordering was observed under thread_model 1 and 2 but only 1 is pinned.

decisions.point: Display settings persistence and kernel state (T2, T3, TD-04, TD-26)
decisions.chosen: DisplaySettings persisted host-locally by the Chart Table SettingsStore (CT-19, ADR-0030); ADR-0006 is not a dependency; kernel state and the restore CUT come from PresentationClock.state and load_seq; no KernelStateView
decisions.reason: Settings are per-install, not PROFILE or WORLD scope, and ADR-0006 ships zero PROFILE blocks at MVP; the ADR-0001 amendment batch supplies the read-only fields.

decisions.chosen: Only mechanism is the kernel's snap_baseline on entry to RUNNING plus the camera CUT on DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE; the post_restore/ADR-0016 rule is dropped
decisions.reason: Two mechanisms for one guarantee invite double handling or skipped owners.

registry_candidates.name: renderer_and_windows_driver
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: renderer_and_windows_driver
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed; PROVISIONAL until lighting spike steps 1, 2, 9 and pipeline spike steps 11, 12
    api: "rendering/renderer/rendering_method = forward_plus; rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = vulkan and driver.linuxbsd = vulkan, asserted by effective ProjectSettings value in CI and by the live driver name at boot; required keys fallback_to_opengl3 = false and fallback_to_d3d12 = false (fallback_to_vulkan = false if the D3D12 reversal is taken); rendering/driver/threads/thread_model held at default 1 and asserted; a release build treats a method or driver mismatch as a fatal unsupported-GPU screen"
    not: "Compatibility or Mobile renderer; Direct3D 12 on Windows unless the spike tie-break fires (Vulkan fails a correctness check D3D12 passes, or D3D12 beats Vulkan P99 CPU frame time by >= 10 % on RM-DESKTOP); relying on the engine default driver; silent driver fallback; thread_model 2; a release build that logs a wrong method and continues"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    reason: "Forward+ for Light2D and glow parity and the gated HDR contingency (Compatibility ignores use_hdr_2d, probed); RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK are specified in Vulkan terms; a key-absent project reports vulkan on 4.7.2 (windowed probe) while the reference says D3D12 since 4.6, so only an effective-value assertion is safe; the fallback keys default true and would silently ship a Compatibility look"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: world_viewport_wiring
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: world_viewport_wiring
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    api: "Root Window content_scale_mode DISABLED; world SubViewport (size field_px under pass A, field_px * k_z with size_2d_override = field_px and size_2d_override_stretch = true under pass B; use_hdr_2d = false at MVP; UPDATE_ONCE mandatory on any resize while UPDATE_DISABLED, desired mode tracked in ViewportWiring) inside a SubViewportContainer (stretch false, scale (k_z, k_z) under A, texture_filter NEAREST, material null at MVP); CanvasLayers hold 1, HUD 2 (scale (H, H)), MenuPixel 3, MenuReading 4, Debug 5, distinct indices; ViewportWiring.Mode {A, B} is a constructor argument, pass A built at MVP; all written only by PipelineRoot / ViewportWiring"
    not: "root canvas_items / integer stretch to obtain k, H or k_z; SubViewportContainer.stretch_shrink as the primary (floors, 3840/7 gives 548); a pass-B viewport sized to the window (an override that does not divide the size gives a non-integer scale); a Control under the world viewport; two CanvasLayers sharing an index; reading render_target_update_mode back as state; Mode as a const read inside the class"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    reason: "Probed: root integer stretch is exact only at H = k and the default zoom; CanvasLayer.scale and a stretch=false container scale give exact independent integers; an override that does not divide the size gives 2.0029 not 2; a resize of a disabled viewport blanks it; same-index layers rely on a sibling-order tie-break"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: world_viewport_sdr_at_mvp
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: world_viewport_sdr_at_mvp
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed; HDR decided by lighting spike steps 7 and 8
    api: "World SubViewport use_hdr_2d = false and root rendering/viewport/hdr_2d = false at MVP, so palette fills read back exact; the HDR path (use_hdr_2d = true) is adopted only by amending ADR-0008 together with a mandatory PipelineRoot-owned resolve material in the container slot (exact linear-to-sRGB plus a clamp or tonemap policy, included by the Filter shader, gated on the effective rendering method, absent under Compatibility); windowed palette read-back test per renderer"
    not: "use_hdr_2d = true on a viewport drawn through a SubViewportContainer without a resolve (outputs unconverted linear colour: (128,64,200) reads (55,13,147)); a resolve under Compatibility (double-converts to (188,137,229)); use_debanding unless flat fills read back bit-exact with it on"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    reason: "Windowed probe 4.7.2 Forward+: an HDR viewport on the SDR root is not sRGB-converted; Compatibility silently ignores use_hdr_2d, so the fix is renderer-specific"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: zoom_via_logical_size

registry_candidates.name: camera_canvas_transform_write
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: camera_canvas_transform_write
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed; ordering probed on a 4.7.2 dev build, release export UNVERIFIED (spike step 12)
    api: "CameraSolver.solve runs in the CAMERA_SOLVE stage (ADR-0009 stage 1) of PipelineRoot._process and publishes pose_q, f_q, jolt, parallax offsets and the world_to_hud inputs; the CameraHost RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw handler only writes the world SubViewport canvas_transform and the parallax offsets from the solved values (idempotent, branch-free, safe if skipped); primary variant has no Camera2D in the world tree; fallback if step 12 rejects the hook: the write moves to the last statement of PipelineRoot._process after driver.frame (no new ProcessPriority constant)"
    not: "solving inside the frame_pre_draw handler (HUD, Avatar presenter and mouse_to_world_aim would read the previous frame's pose); a Camera2D scroll on its own clock; Camera2D.limit_*; a camera parented to a body; any writer other than the pipeline root, ViewportWiring or the camera host; subscribers drawing from their own _process; ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION_LATE"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    reason: "Probed: frame_pre_draw fires after every _process and before the draw, so a solve in it is invisible to the HUD stage; a write in the handler or in _process is drawn the same frame"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: canvas_coordinate_exactness
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: canvas_coordinate_exactness
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    api: "Presentation coordinates are integer-valued float32, exact for |v| <= 2^24 base px; Vector2i is converted to Vector2 only at Placement.put and at the canvas_transform write; pose_q is Vector2i quantised from the solver's float64 scalars before that conversion; world and body-frame extents stay below 2^24 base px (ADR-0015 owns the bound if body-frame extents could exceed it; the rebase mechanism keeps coordinates inside it); unit test at 2^24 - 1, 2^24 and 2^24 + 1"
    not: "a non-integer-valued presentation coordinate; silent float32 rounding of a canvas origin"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    reason: "Transform2D, Node2D.position and Control.position are float32 in the standard build; closes the float32 canvas exactness reference of ADR-0005 TR-shipbody-038 and ADR-0010"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: viewport_geometry_written_outside_pipeline_root
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: viewport_geometry_written_outside_pipeline_root
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    description: "Only PipelineRoot and ViewportWiring (src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd) write SubViewport.size and size_2d_override*, the world container's position, scale, stretch_shrink and material, any CanvasLayer scale, offset or transform, and HudRoot.size; only the CameraHost frame_pre_draw handler writes the world canvas_transform and the parallax offsets; no subscriber, the Filter, Lighting, HUD or Chart Table writes a viewport or camera property; no code but RenderLayout.derive computes k, H, world_to_hud or the cursor mapping."
    why: "Two writers or a re-derived projection produce fractional transforms and disagreeing HUD anchors (TR-pxl-003, TR-pxl-019); the pixel-integrity promise needs one source."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: root_stretch_or_camera2d_zoom_for_scale
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: root_stretch_or_camera2d_zoom_for_scale
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    description: "No root canvas_items or integer stretch to obtain k, H or k_z; no Camera2D.zoom, no tweened or non-integer scale, no Control.scale on HUD nodes, no scale animation anywhere in the world or HUD."
    why: "Root stretch is exact only when H equals k at the default zoom (probed), so it cannot host the Deck's world 2x and HUD 3x; non-integer scale is the failure the pipeline exists to prevent."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: control_or_reading_text_under_world_or_scaled_layer
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: control_or_reading_text_under_world_or_scaled_layer
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    description: "No Control and no node in group hud under the world SubViewport; no reading-face (vector) text under an integer-scaled CanvasLayer or the world container; reading-face text lives on a scale (1,1) layer (MenuReadingLayer, layer 4) with sizes in screen px; HUD text uses bitmap faces or configured oversampling."
    why: "A Control under the world receives world light and the Filter (HR-1); text under an integer scale is bitmap-stretched and blurs."

    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: render_mode_branch_outside_viewport_wiring

registry_candidates.name: camera_solve_inside_frame_pre_draw
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: camera_solve_inside_frame_pre_draw
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed
    description: "CameraSolver.solve is called only from the CAMERA_SOLVE stage inside PipelineRoot._process; the frame_pre_draw handler performs the two canvas writes from already-solved values and never solves; no presenter defines its own _process; PipelineRoot is the only PresentationHost."
    why: "frame_pre_draw fires after every _process (probed), so a solve in it leaves world_to_hud, the beam pose and the aim mapping one frame behind the world (PR-6 C11, TR-pxl-019)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: silent_renderer_or_driver_fallback
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: silent_renderer_or_driver_fallback
    status: active           # ADR-0008 is Proposed

decisions.chosen: Option (a): use_hdr_2d=false at MVP, container material null, flat-palette guarantee kept; option (b) specified as a gated contingency (resolve material included by the Filter shader, gated on the effective rendering method, D_filter becomes 1)
decisions.reason: Probed: an HDR viewport through a container on the SDR root outputs unconverted linear colour ((128,64,200) reads (55,13,147)); the resolve fix is renderer-specific (double-converts under Compatibility). (a) keeps every other ADR rule consistent until lighting spike steps 7 and 8 prove HDR is needed.

decisions.point: Presentation host and camera solve placement (E2, T1, TD-03)
decisions.chosen: PipelineRoot is the single PresentationHost; one _process at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION runs present_time, zoom cooldown, RESCALING, driver.frame; CameraSolver.solve is the CAMERA_SOLVE stage; frame_pre_draw only writes canvas_transform and parallax offsets; PRESENTATION_LATE withdrawn
decisions.reason: Probed: frame_pre_draw fires after every _process, so a solve inside it would leave the HUD, beam pose and aim mapping one frame behind the world; this also removes the priority tie and keeps the solver unit-testable headless.

decisions.chosen: Distinct indices: hold 1, HUD 2, MenuPixel 3, MenuReading 4, Debug 5
decisions.reason: Removes the dependency on a sibling-order tie-break that is fragile to reparenting; no test needed.

decisions.chosen: Pipeline GDD D.16 owns the figures; ADR-0008 7 owns the rules and keeps a mirrored table; container composite is its own row; D_root 63 and 93; DrawBudget.validate dropped
decisions.reason: A Foundation ADR must not churn after every spike measurement; the composite draw is counted on the root (probed). A separate frame-budget.md was out of scope for a single-file pass.

decisions.chosen: Pass A built at MVP behind ViewportWiring.Mode, a constructor argument; pass B and the A/B equivalence test are built only if lighting spike step 2 adopts B; debug tree walk is an optional later story
decisions.reason: A GDScript const cannot be varied in a test, and B is not yet adopted.

decisions.chosen: fallback_to_opengl3=false and fallback_to_d3d12=false are required project.godot keys; a release-build method/driver mismatch is a fatal unsupported-GPU screen; thread_model held at 1
decisions.reason: The engine defaults all fallbacks to true and would silently ship a Compatibility look; the probed hook ordering was observed under thread_model 1 and 2 but only 1 is pinned.

decisions.point: Display settings persistence and kernel state (T2, T3, TD-04, TD-26)
decisions.chosen: DisplaySettings persisted host-locally by the Chart Table SettingsStore (CT-19, ADR-0030); ADR-0006 is not a dependency; kernel state and the restore CUT come from PresentationClock.state and load_seq; no KernelStateView
decisions.reason: Settings are per-install, not PROFILE or WORLD scope, and ADR-0006 ships zero PROFILE blocks at MVP; the ADR-0001 amendment batch supplies the read-only fields.

decisions.chosen: Only mechanism is the kernel's snap_baseline on entry to RUNNING plus the camera CUT on DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE; the post_restore/ADR-0016 rule is dropped
decisions.reason: Two mechanisms for one guarantee invite double handling or skipped owners.

decisions.chosen: File grew from about 95 KB to about 161 KB, mostly the mandated Registry Candidates section (TD-33) and the added probe record
decisions.reason: T7 flagged size; the growth is required content, not a decline, and the section can be trimmed once the orchestrator merges the candidates into the registry.

open_questions: OQ-A: renderer method and Windows driver stay provisional until lighting spike steps 1, 2, 9 and pipeline spike steps 11 and 12 have run; the technical director rules on a reversal.

OQ-B: scaled stretch=false SubViewportContainer sampling for textured content, a one-pixel checker, pass B (if built), an odd window size, fractional container position, Compatibility and a release export (flat fill already passes).

OQ-C: the reference says D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6, but a key-absent 4.7.2 project reports vulkan; likely a new-project-template value (UNVERIFIED); reference corrections suggested for modules/rendering.md and breaking-changes.md.

OQ-G (this ADR's letter): whether a disabled viewport holds its last texture when no resize occurs (the PAUSED_FROZEN hold); the resize case is resolved by probe. Not to be confused with ADR-0009's OQ-G/OQ-A letters.

OQ-H: whether the ambient floor and glow can be met with the world viewport SDR, or require use_hdr_2d=true with the section 2.4 resolve material (lighting spike steps 7 and 8); art bible 8.4 and the Lighting GDD need the matching correction.

External dependency (not an OQ): ADR-0001's amendment batch must land PresentationClock.state, PresentationClock.load_seq and ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE before this ADR can be Accepted; ADR-0007, ADR-0009 and ADR-0010 must be Accepted or co-accepted.

Routing note: TD-22's references to OQ-G (TR-pc-039) going to the Player Controller GDD owner and OQ-A's GDD half going to the HUD GDD owner are ADR-0009's OQ letters, not this ADR's, so this pass did not route them.

Release export, Direct3D 12, Steam Deck, a minimised or occluded window and low_processor_mode remain UNVERIFIED for the frame_pre_draw hook (pipeline spike step 12); all draw-call and timing figures remain unmeasured.
